'''Serge Belamant''' (born 1953) is a French-born South African entrepreneur best known for designing the Universal Electronic [[Payment system|Payment System]] (UEPS) and the Chip Offline Pre-authorised Card (COPAC).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/cell-c-ma-blue-label/update-3-south-africas-blue-label-pays-400-mln-for-cell-c-stake-idUSL5N1CB15X/|title=South Africa's Blue Label pays $400 mln for Cell C stake|date=2016-10-27|website=Reuters}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.finsmes.com/2020/08/net1-technologies-and-its-history-of-financial-technology-innovation.html|title=Net1 Technologies and Its History of Financial Technology Innovation|date=2020-08-30|website=Finsmes}}</ref>

He founded the cash-payments company Net1 UEPS Technologies in 1989, led it through dual listings on the [[NASDAQ]] and the [[Johannesburg Stock Exchange]], and oversaw the contentious welfare-payments contract with the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) until his retirement in 2017.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-05-25 |title=Net1 Founder to Quit After South African Welfare Controversy |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2017-05-25/net1-founder-to-retire-after-south-african-welfare-controversy?embedded-checkout=true |access-date=2024-12-27 |work=Bloomberg.com |language=en}}</ref> Since 2018 he has been non-executive chair of London-based buy-now-pay-later fintech Zilch.<ref name=":0" />

== Early life and education ==
Belamant moved from France to South Africa with his family in 1967 and matriculated from Highlands North Boys' High School, Johannesburg.{{Citation needed|date=April 2026}} In 1972 he entered the [[University of the Witwatersrand]] to study civil engineering but switched to computer science and [[applied mathematics]] in his second year. He left the university without a degree and later took short courses in information systems at the [[University of South Africa]] (UNISA).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.f6s.com/member/sergebelamant|title=Serge Belamant's Profile|website=F6S}}</ref>

== Early career and SASWITCH (1981–1989) ==
Belamant worked for [[Control Data Corporation]] as a systems analyst for a decade before joining SASWITCH Ltd in 1985.{{Citation needed|date=April 2026}}  Economic sanctions had left the consortium's national ATM network dependent on unsupported Christian Rovsing computers.<ref name="BizNewsInterview">{{cite interview |interviewer=Alec Hogg |title=Net1's Serge Belamant: "Business is ugly—disrupt at your peril" |url=https://www.biznews.com/entrepreneur/net1s-serge-belamant-business-is-ugly-disrupt-at-your-reputational-peril |access-date=10 July 2025 |work=BizNews |date=9 Aug 2016}}</ref> Belamant led a rebuild on fault-tolerant Stratus hardware and wrote protocol-translation software that allowed fourteen banks to connect without altering their host systems.<ref name="CompCom2008">{{cite report |url=https://www.compcom.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/5-ATMs-and-direct-charging_non-confidential1.pdf |title=Banking Enquiry Report to the Competition Commissioner – Chapter 5: ATMs and Direct Charging |date=June 2008 |publisher=Competition Commission of South Africa |access-date=2025-07-10}}</ref>

By 1988 SASWITCH was handling about three million ATM transactions a month, according to the Competition Commission.<ref name="BizNewsInterview" /> The switch—now run by BankservAfrica—remains the backbone of South Africa's shared ATM network.<ref name=":2" />

== Net1 UEPS Technologies (1989–2017) ==

=== Founding and UEPS ===
In 1989, Serge Belamant developed the Universal Electronic Payment System (UEPS), enabling secure, real-time transactions even in areas with limited connectivity. In the same year, he founded NET1 UEPS Technologies Inc., serving as its CEO and Director.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.theexeterdaily.co.uk/news/business/serge-belamant%E2%80%99s-track-record-improving-society-through-technology|title=Serge Belamant's Track Record Improving Society Through Technology|website=The Exeter Daily|date=24 July 2020 }}</ref>

=== COPAC for VISA ===
In 1995, VISA tasked Belamant with designing the Chip Offline Pre-authorized Card (COPAC), a technology still widely used in chip-enabled credit and debit cards.{{Citation needed|date=April 2026}} A year later, he listed his company APLITEC (Applied Technology Holdings Limited) on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-08-30/net-1-ceo-says-doesn-t-care-about-south-african-court-challenge|title=Net1 CEO Says Doesn't Care About South African Court Challenge|website=Bloomberg}}</ref>

=== Listings and acquisitions ===
In 1999, Belamant acquired Cash Payment Services (CPS) from First National Bank of South Africa, modernizing its welfare payment system to serve millions in rural areas.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.finsmes.com/2020/08/net1-technologies-and-its-history-of-financial-technology-innovation.html|title=Net1 Technologies and Its History of Financial Technology Innovation|website=Finsmes|date=20 August 2020 }}</ref> In 2005, he led NET1 Technologies to an IPO, listing it as NET1 UEPS Technologies Inc. on the Nasdaq. A secondary listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) followed in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.businesslive.co.za/fm/features/cover-story/2021-03-18-can-net1-be-rehabilitated-after-its-social-grants-tender-debacle/|title=Can Net1 Be Rehabilitated After Its Social Grants Tender Debacle?|website=BusinessLive}}</ref>

=== SASSA contract ===
Under Belamant's leadership, NET1 managed welfare payments for the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA), handling payments for over 10 million beneficiaries monthly.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.saflii.org/za/cases/ZASCA/2019/131.html|title=SASSA Contract Judgment|website=SAFLII}}</ref> Despite criticism over handling the SASSA contract, investigations by the [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Department of Justice]] and the South African Constitutional Court found no wrongdoing.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.europeanbusinessreview.com/the-legacy-of-serge-belamant-and-net1-technologies/|title=The Legacy of Serge Belamant and Net1 Technologies|website=European Business Review|date=27 October 2020 }}</ref>

== Zilch (2018–present) ==
Belamant co-founded London-based "buy-now-pay-later" firm Zilch Technology in 2018 and serves as non-executive chair.<ref name=":0" /> Zilch reported £145 million in annual-recurring revenue and 4.5 million customers in January 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bmmagazine.co.uk/business/how-philip-belamant-ceo-and-co-founder-of-revolutionary-payments-venture-zilch-has-disrupted-the-fintech-space/|title=How Zilch Has Disrupted the Fintech Space|website=Business Matters|date=6 September 2022 }}</ref>

== Patents ==
Belamant is listed as inventor on more than a dozen payment-security patents, including:

* "Funds transfer system" (US RE36,788, 2000) – the basis for UEPS.<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Biometric electromechanical credential|pubdate=2014-03-13|url=https://worldwide.espacenet.com/textdoc?DB=EPODOC&IDX=WO2014037869A1|WO|2014037869A1|date=|access-date=}}</ref>
* "Financial transactions with a varying PIN" (WO 2014/037869, 2014).<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Self-decodable indicia marking for automatic machine reading|pubdate=2000-04-18|url=https://worldwide.espacenet.com/textdoc?DB=EPODOC&IDX=USRE36788E|US|RE36788E|date=|access-date=}}</ref>
